subject: Implementing Brier score and other loss functions for logistic regression and occupancy models in NIMBLE

messages.author: 54dcd7303f9accde
messages.subject: Implementing Brier score and other loss functions for logistic regression and occupancy models in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi,

Hope this email is finding you well. I have been trying to compute the different predictive performance metrics used in Broms et al. (2010) as a model selection criteria in occupancy models using k-fold cross-validation. (Broms, K. M., Hooten, M. B., & Fitzpatrick, R. M. (2016). Model selection and assessment for multi‐species occupancy models. Ecology, 97(7), 1759-1770.)  I think NIMBLE can be a great tool to implement such metrics ina computationally efficient way.

I begin by computing the Brier score based on the (1) detection-non detection data left out in each fold and retained as the validation data, and (2) the unconditional probability of detection (i.e, the probability that a species is present and detected) estimated from the subsamples used in the training data. Similarly, I computed the 0-1 score based on the posterior predictive values and the known-out-of-sample data values.

My first take on this was to use the runCrossValidate() function to compute the  0-1 score but I don't know if a different loss function (e.g. the ones commonly used for logistic regression) could be used such as AUC, Brier score, log-loss, etc. Thus, I  Implemented a 5-fold cross-validation manually by defining a nimble function that plugs in the posterior estimates of each MCMC sample to simulate the response values in each fold and compared them against the true values in the out-of-sample data (or compute the brier score based on the unconditional detection probability). However, I encountered a few problems that hopefully you can help me with.

(1) The results from using the runCrossValidate() function and the manual approach are slightly different and I am not sure if this could be because of the random allocation or because I am specifying something wrong in the runCrossValidate argument (especially with the dimensions). I tried different seeds and the results are still somewhat different.

(2)  the manual approach works when folds are of the same size because I can simply change the data values in a loop without recompiling the model in each fold. I don't think there is a way of avoiding recompiling the model each time when the size between folds is different right? (because the size in the training and test sets are declared as constant in the operational model)

(3) I defined a nimble function for defining the loss function scores and tried to use it in my second nimble function to compute the actual scores after simulating the data set. However, when I try to compile the second function I get an error that says failed to create a shared library. In the meantime, I defined the loss function directly into my second nimble function using simple R operations supported for NIMBLE but it would be great if you could help me to understand what am I doing wrong by implementing a user-defined function within the run argument of another nimble function.

I have attached a reproducible code. 

Many thanks,

Jafet

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Implementing Brier score and other loss functions for logistic regression and occupancy models in NIMBLE
parts:
Hi Jafet,

Thanks for the questions.  This sounds interesting.

runCrossValidate has a good bit of room to be generalized one day, so indeed you might run into some limitations.

For using a different loss function, have you tried working with the lossFunction argument (see help(runCrossValidate))?  It can be simply an R function (not necessarily a nimbleFunction).  However you may already be past that point.

I'm not sure what would cause your different results.  Even with different seeds, it seems likely that the exact order of any random number draws is not the same between your code and nimble's code, so I would only expect a statistical match, not exactly matched numbers.  I did not run and study the differences.

You are correct that the model needs to be recompiled for each fold.  There are slicker ways to work around this, but they are not automated in runCrossValidate, and you have already built your own tools.

I did not run all of your code (thanks for providing it simply and clearly), but I did succeed in the three compileNimble calls on lines 200-205, including the clossSampler.  Is this the one that wasn't working for you?  That's what I am guessing from what you described, so I am not sure where there is a reproducible compilation failure.  There have been some bug fixes recently so I can give the generic suggestion to be sure you've updated nimble.  Otherwise can you say more about where there is a reproducible compilation failure in your code?

Best wishes,
Perry
